title: Polynomial-time reverse length comparison
statement: For all $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, the function on binary strings that sends $z$ to the one-bit string containing $1$ exactly when $C(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^c\le |\pi_2(z)|$, and containing $0$ otherwise, is polynomial-time computable. Here each projection returns the corresponding component when $z$ is a valid encoded pair and the empty string otherwise.
replaced:
For a binary string $z$, let $\pi_1(z)$ and $\pi_2(z)$ be the two components $a$
and $b$ when $z = \langle a, b\rangle$ is a well-formed self-delimiting pair
encoding ($a$ with every bit doubled, then $01$, then $b$), and let both be the
empty string otherwise. Then for all $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$, the map sending $z$ to
the one-bit string recording whether $C(|\pi_1(z)|+1)^c \le |\pi_2(z)|$ is
polynomial-time computable: some finite multi-tape Turing machine over the binary
alphabet computes it within $D(n+1)^d$ steps on every input of length $n$, for
some constants $D, d \in \mathbb{N}$.
